entries.en: If we're lucky, we'll actually realize usable technology from this study in a few years.
Please let me know if you have any other questions.
This is a long-term study. I wouldn't expect the bodies to be released for a year or longer.
Very few bodies had this new type of weapon damage, and very few were in good enough condition to study.
Beyond that, Commander, we need as many bodies as we can to get a reasonable sample size.
I'm sorry, Commander. The needs of the living outweigh the needs of the dead.
The military has made its choice, and it believes that gaining new technology is worth inconveniencing people like Mr. Bhatia.
Studying Nirali Bhatia's body could save the lives of countless soldiers. I can't release her.
Commander, I-- I don't think threats are necessary.
Even if the body were here on the Citadel, would you really risk going in shooting to get it?
Commander, you of all people should understand how far we must go to protect humanity!
All right, Commander. You win. It was hard enough refusing Mr. Bhatia. I'm not going to risk an incident by refusing you.
Tell Samesh that the body is being shipped back to Earth. I'll go now to see to it myself.
My goodness, you're Commander Shepard!
Your activities made for quite a briefing in the Diplomatic Corps! Is there something I can do to assist you?
Ah, Mr. Bhatia. A good man in an understandably frustrating position. I wish I could help him.
Commander, nothing would make me happier. I'm afraid, though, that it's not quite that simple.
Serviceman Nirali Bhatia died on Eden Prime, as Mr. Bhatia no doubt told you.
Her wounds are inconsistent with any type of weapon damage we've seen before. That is why her body is being held.
We are not holding Nirali Bhatia's body out of discretion. We are, frankly, holding the body for research.
No, Commander. Nirali Bhatia is not dangerous. Her body is, in fact, extremely valuable to the Alliance.
The tests we are conducting may lead to better defenses against geth attacks.
Respectfully, Serviceman Bhatia may save more lives in death than she did in life.
That was just the reaction we were hoping to avoid, Commander.
But if you think it will help, tell Mr. Bhatia the truth. Perhaps he will understand.
Thank you. I appreciate that.
When will this research result in actual new technology?
How long do you think the research is going to take?
You've got to have a lot of bodies. Can't you release one?
Thanks for your help.
I'd like you to reconsider releasing Nirali Bhatia's body.
You've got no legal right to keep the body, and I know you don't want this to go public.
You know who and what I am. If I want Nirali Bhatia, I can get her.
You said you'd been briefed on me. You should know that I don't leave fallen troops behind.
You said you'd been briefed on me. How do you think I feel about people mistreating the dead?
You said you'd been briefed on me. How far do you think I'm willing to go on this?
The marine's name was Nirali Bhatia. If you want to cut her up, you call her by name.
I understand what you're trying to do, but holding the body is wrong.
Not if we lose our humanity in the process! I'm out there fighting to stop crap like this!
You've read my file. You know how far I'm willing to go, and I'm telling you to release the body.
Is this what I'm out there fighting for? A government that steals the bodies of its honored dead?
Soldiers shouldn't have to worry about what their own government is going to do to their bodies.
Yes. A man named Samesh Bhatia is having some trouble claiming his wife's body.
You can cut the red tape for a grieving husband. I want you to release the body of Nirali Bhatia.
I'm here on behalf of Samesh Bhatia for his wife, Nirali.
I don't care how badly the geth mangled the body. It's the husband's right to claim her.
You think that her body might be dangerous or contaminated?
You're studying her injuries to learn more about geth weaponry.
I'll tell Samesh. Next time you cut up a dead soldier, at least tell her husband the truth.
I'll tell Mr. Bhatia about this. It might make it easier for him to understand.
Results of Research
Length of Research
Number of Bodies
Please help Samesh.
Release the body. Now.
Thanks for the information.
I'm releasing the body.
She deserves better.
Her. Not it, her.
I do, and you're wrong.
It's not worth it.
Not this far.
At what cost?
You're betraying the dead.
I'm here for Samesh.
Stop stealing corpses.
So she's been mauled.
She's toxic?
You're running tests.
Samesh should hear this.
I'll pass this on.
So they finally did it? I knew one of your kind would make Spectre one day.
Was there something you needed, Commander?
I'll be going now.
No, I just don't trust your kind. Not yet.
You humans are eager to take all the power you can get. And you're being given a lot.
If the Council wants to make humanity their new favorite pet, that's their business. But I don't have to like it.
Good. Then fight for it. But don't expect the rest of us to just sit back and let you take it.
I'm a busy man, Commander. Are we done here?
C-Sec provides necessary police and security services throughout the Citadel.
We're a civilian government agency, though many of our members have had military training.
I've been with C-Sec for thirty years. I've never had to break the law to do my job. Not once.
Spectres walk a slippery slope, Commander. Operate outside the law and it changes you. Look what happened to Saren.
Yeah, right. You expect us to believe none of your officers are corrupt?
You expect us to believe none of your officers are corrupt?
That is not a completely accurate analogy, Executor. You cannot deny that some C-Sec officers are corrupt.
Don't piss in my ear and tell me it's raining. I've known plenty of dirty C-Sec agents.
There are over two hundred thousand C-Sec agents. Some of them are going to be bad. But we don't turn a blind eye to corruption like the Spectres do.
We do our best to find and punish any officer who breaks the law. Spectres -- they'll never come under that kind of scrutiny.
I agree, but they need to be held to a higher standard. They need to be accountable.
Saren's out of control. We both know that. But because he's a Spectre, the Council doesn't want to do anything about it.
They're the right hand of the Council, or so they like to be called.
More like the underhanded side of the Council.
I get the feeling you're not too fond of humans.
The Council treats us like second-class citizens. We have to fight for everything we get.
Tell me about C-Sec.
Sometimes you have to bend the law to keep people safe.
The galaxy needs people like that, people who do the dirty jobs.
Attitude towards humans
We're not favorites!
That's a bit naïve.
Spectres are important.
Commander Shepard. I didn't expect to see you here. Did Ambassador Udina send you?
You humans are always so curious. Always sticking your fingers into someone else's pie. Is that the right expression?
Uh, never mind. Forget I asked.
Sorry, Commander. I don't make a habit of giving out details about ongoing investigations.
Have we met before?
I came on my own. I need information.
Nobody sends me anywhere. I just need some information.
Tell me about your investigation into Saren.
Then can you tell me what you know about Garrus?
I go where I want.
Investigation
Garrus.
Is that the kind of person this galaxy needs?
True. I hope that's something you'll take to heart, Shepard.
True, but the potential is always there.
If the cure is worse than the disease... what's the point?
Maybe. But I've never had to cross that line to get the job done. Never.
Of course, as the C-Sec representative to the Council, I spend most of my time liaising between the two.
I can't abide any organization that considers itself above the law.
Especially when it's left up to each individual Spectre to decide when and how to "bend the rules".
Garrus Vakarian? Good officer. Very good in fact. But he needs to learn some patience.
You'd think an officer of the law would be a bit more mindful of rules and regulations--
Shepard. What can I do for you now?
I only hope you're better than the one they're sending you after.
Hmm. That's what worries me.
Was there something you wanted?
Why did you come to see me, Shepard? Did Ambassador Udina send you?
No. But I know you well enough. I'm Executor Pallin, head of C-Sec.
It's my job to know when someone like you arrives on the Citadel.
And, unlike the Spectres, we work within the bounds of the law.
I'll do everything I can to stop Saren.
But not all Spectres are like Saren.
Absolutely. The only thing that matters is accomplishing the task.
What do you have against the Spectres?
If it gets the job done.
You don't like them?
I strive to be.
And you're the first human Spectre. Get used to people knowing who you are, at least around here.
This place seems strange. I wish there were more humans around.
You have to be tough with these aliens. They won't respect you otherwise.
It's good to see another human face around here.
If I have to listen to another hanar take twenty minutes to say the simplest thing, I think I'll scream.
Don't believe the rumors. The Consort would never reveal her secrets.
Of course she wouldn't. She'd be tossed out the nearest airlock if she did.
Besides, Nick, the Consort's nothing like the girls back on the colonies. She's.... She's....
You don't have to do it with her. You can just talk to her if you want.
Is that all you did, Jaz? Just talk?
I didn't say that!
